_meta.title: Self-host PaaS recommendations — deploy_shape signal → PaaS map
_meta.derived_from: ai-kit internal catalog (not vendored from upstream)
_meta.notes: Catalogues open-source self-host PaaS layers surfaced by /ai:recommend-tools and /ai:setup when bin/detect-tooling.sh reports deploy_shape=self-host. v1 ships Coolify-only — the user-validated path on naschool/emeq. Dokku (single-host buildpack), Caprover (Swarm cluster), and Kamal (CLI-driven) deferred to follow-up issues so the catalog grows from real adoption signal, not speculation. Preview-then-confirm: ai-kit never writes Docker/server config without explicit user approval.

recommendations.name: coolify
recommendations.best_for: Docker-shaped projects that have outgrown Vercel/Railway/fly.io and want a UI-driven self-host PaaS on their own VPS
recommendations.value: Heroku-style git-push deploys + UI for environments, services, databases, backups. Built on Docker (no Swarm/Kubernetes overhead). Coolify MCP server available — when wired, the agent can list/deploy/inspect Coolify resources directly.
recommendations.risk: Medium — self-hosted control plane; user owns ops + upgrades. AGPL-3.0 is viral for Coolify itself but does not affect deployed projects (deploying via Coolify is not 'distributing' Coolify).

tradeoffs.vs_alternatives: Dokku (CLI, buildpack, single-host) · Caprover (UI, Docker Swarm cluster) · Kamal (CLI-only, 37signals' Capistrano-style). Coolify wins on UI + DX; loses to Kamal on simplicity + GitOps and to Dokku on resource footprint.

install.post_recommend_action: Open coolify.io/docs/installation in browser; ai-kit never writes Docker/server config without explicit approval.
